chunks: The venerable Sheikh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Rashid narrated to us. He said: Abu Ma'mar Sa'id ibn Khaytham narrated to us. He said: Sa'd narrated to me from al-Hasan al-Basri,

that it reached him that someone was claiming to be diminishing Ali (peace be upon him). So he stood among his companions one day and said: I was determined to lock my door and not leave my house until death comes to me. I was informed that one of you claims that I diminish the best of people after our Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) — his companion and intimate, the one who relieved distress in times of calamity, and the slayer of adversaries on the day of combat.

A man has departed from you who recited the Quran and revered it, who acquired knowledge and preserved it, who possessed valor and employed it in obedience to his Lord — patient in the bitterness of war, grateful in hardship and distress. He acted by the Book of his Lord and gave sincere counsel to his Prophet, his cousin, and his brother. He was made his brother above all his companions, and he was entrusted with his secret. He strove for him in youth and fought alongside him in maturity. He slew adversaries and brought down knights in defense of God's religion, until war laid down its burdens. He held fast to the covenant of his Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) — no one could turn him aside, no opponent could sway him. Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) passed away while he was pleased with him.

The most knowledgeable of Muslims in learning, the most understanding in comprehension, and the foremost in embracing Islam — none equals him in his virtues, none resembles him in his qualities. His soul was restrained from desires; he worked for God in moments of heedlessness; he perfected ritual purity in cold mornings; he was humble in prayers; he cut himself off from pleasures, exerting himself strenuously — of noble character and noble lineage. He followed the practices of his Prophet and traced the footsteps of his Master. So how could I say anything about him that would doom me?! No one I know finds fault with him. So spare us harm and avoid the path of perdition.

key_terms.التَّنَازُلِ: The day of combat/battle — refers to the fierce single combats (mubara'a) in which Ali excelled
key_terms.الرَّدَى: Perdition, destruction — al-Hasan's warning against those who would speak ill of Ali
key_terms.الزَّلَازِلِ: Earthquakes/calamities — metaphor for the critical crises of early Islam when Ali's support was indispensable
key_terms.السَّبَرَاتُ: Cold mornings — referring to the discipline of performing ritual purity in harsh conditions
key_terms.اللَّأْوَاءُ: Hardship, deprivation — an archaic Arabic term for severe trials
key_terms.خَيْرَ النَّاسِ: The best of people — a well-known designation for Imam Ali used in early Islamic discourse
key_terms.ضَرَائِبُ: Natural qualities, inherent traits — referring to inborn character

ai.seo_question: What did al-Hasan al-Basri say about Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib?
ai.summary: Al-Hasan al-Basri (d. 110 AH), a famous Tabi'i scholar revered across Muslim communities, publicly defended Imam Ali (AS) against a person in his circle who allegedly claimed al-Hasan was belittling Ali. This speech is remarkable because al-Hasan al-Basri, generally considered part of the early Sunni scholarly tradition, here delivers an eloquent and passionate encomium of Ali ibn Abi Talib, praising his Quranic devotion, his knowledge, his courage, his asceticism, and his unmatched rank after the Prophet. The narration is transmitted through Sheikh al-Saduq, placing it within Shia hadith literature as evidence that even non-Shia early scholars recognized Ali's supreme virtue.

en.bilal-muhammad: Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b Ishaq (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Jarir al-Tabari narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Rashid narrated to us. He said: Abu Mu`ammar Sa`id b. Khaytham narrated to us. He said: Sa`d narrated to me from al-Hasan al-Basri.

He was informed that someone was claiming that he was diminishing [the status of] `Ali (as). So, he stood among his companions one day and said: I was worried that my door would be locked and that I would not leave my house until my term (death) had come. I was informed that one of you had claimed that I was diminishing the best of people after our Prophet (s), who was his gentleman and the one he would sit with; the one who would bring relief to him during earthquakes, and the one who would fight the people during the time of revelation.

A man who recited the Quran and revered it has left you. He seized knowledge and retained it. He withstood hardship and used it in obedience to his Lord. He was patient over the bitterness of war and grateful during deprivation and calamity. He acted by the Book of his Lord and counselled His Prophet, his cousin, and his brother. He was made his brother out of all his companions and imparted his secret to him. He strove on his behalf a little, and he fought alongside him much. He killed the people and brought the knights down below the religion of Allah until the war would come to its end. He grasped onto the covenant of his Prophet (s) without abandoning or opposing it. Then, the Prophet (s) passed away while he was pleased with him. He taught the Muslims knowledge, he made them understand, and he preceded them in Islam. None match his virtues, and none resemble him in his striking.

He freed himself of desires, and he worked for Allah during times of heedlessness. He bathed in purity during cold mornings, and he humbled himself during prayers. He cut himself off from pleasures and strove hard when sent forth. He was goodly in character and noble in lineage. He followed the traditions of his Prophet the most, and he sufficed himself with the sayings of his Master. So, how could I say something regarding him that would not help me?! Stop this harm and avoid the path of evil.
